title: Flutter web Shader compilation error
body: I built my Flutter web app with `flutter build web --web-renderer canvaskit` and published it to Firebase Hosting. The published website does not work and Chrome DevTools reports a shader compilation error, although the app works in debugging mode. My reproduction is at https://github.com/reporter/flutter_webgl_error and the deployed site is https://flutter-webgl-error.web.app. I am using Flutter stable 3.16.4 on an Intel Mac.

symptoms_visible: My published CanvasKit website does not work and the Chrome console reports a shader compilation error, while the same app works in debugging mode.
N0.label: N0 published CanvasKit app fails

symptoms_visible: The deployed app fails in Chrome Beta 121 on my Intel Mac, but it works in the other browsers I tried, including Chrome Stable 120 and Chrome Canary 122.
I only see the failure with the CanvasKit renderer.
N1.label: N1 browser and architecture scope established

symptoms_visible: The same deployed CanvasKit example still fails in the affected Chrome browser when built with Flutter master.
N2.label: N2 Flutter master also affected

symptoms_visible: The failing browser reports `CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL`, invalid WebGL operations, and a shader compilation error for a fragment shader that samples a texture and applies a circle.
After removing the extra code and keeping only my list of circular avatars, the same error still occurs.
N3.label: N3 GPU and shader evidence collected

symptoms_visible: Loading a JPG or JPEG image from the network makes the release app go blank with the shader error on affected Intel Macs, while equivalent PNG, WebP, and GIF images render.
N4.label: N4 network JPEG trigger isolated

symptoms_visible: After enabling Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization and relaunching Chrome, the same hosted example still throws the exception on my affected Intel Mac.
N4_x.label: N4_x canvas rasterization flag aftermath

symptoms_visible: The default release build still fails with network JPEG images, but a profile or release build compiled with `--dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false` renders them.
N5.label: N5 browser image decoding workaround verified

symptoms_visible: I've updated Chrome to 122.0.6261.129; I haven't re-run the avatar page yet.
N6.label: N6 Chrome-side correction verified (fix applied, unverified)

symptoms_visible: The published Flutter CanvasKit website renders normally in the corrected Chrome version on Intel macOS, including its network JPEG images, and the WebGL shader error no longer appears.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

symptoms_visible: I tried the newer Chrome Beta (v123) and the page still goes blank with the same error.
N5_x2.label: N5_x2 newer-beta aftermath

question_patterns: Which browser and exact version reproduce the failure?
Does this happen specifically on your Intel Mac or on other hardware too?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It fails in Chrome Beta 121.0.6167.16, the x86_64 build, on my 2020 Intel MacBook Pro.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails in every browser and on both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs.
It fails on another Chrome 121 x86_64 patch version on the same Intel Mac.

question_patterns: Can you try the deployed site in another browser?
Does the failure reproduce outside Chrome?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried all my other browsers and the site works there. I only see this failure in the affected Chrome build.

question_patterns: What happens in Chrome Stable, Beta, and Canary on the same machine?
Can you compare nearby Chrome release channels?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On the same Intel Mac, Chrome Stable 120 works, Chrome Beta 121 does not work, and Chrome Canary 122 works.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Stable, Beta, and Canary all fail identically on the same machine.

question_patterns: Does this occur only with the CanvasKit renderer?
Can you reproduce it with the HTML renderer too?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, I only see it with CanvasKit rendering.

edges.comment: Thread c1-c12: browser/channel and architecture comparison narrowed the failure to particular Chrome x86_64 builds on Intel macOS and confirmed that the original case uses CanvasKit.

question_patterns: Can you rebuild and test this on the Flutter master channel?
Please test master and provide its `flutter doctor -v` output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested Flutter master 3.18.0-18.0.pre.39 with engine afd214dccc, and I get the same result.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The master build renders correctly in the same affected browser while stable still fails.

edges.comment: Thread c6-c7: a handler-requested channel test showed that moving from stable to current Flutter master did not alter the observation.

question_patterns: Please provide the failing browser's `chrome://gpu` or `about:gpu` output.
What graphics features, GPU workarounds, and ANGLE information does the affected browser report?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My Chrome Beta `about:gpu` output says Canvas, compositing, rasterization, WebGL, and WebGL2 are hardware accelerated. It lists Intel Mac workarounds such as `dont_use_loops_to_initialize_variables`, `disable_webgl_rgb_multisampling_usage`, and `msaa_is_slow`. Canvas out-of-process rasterization is disabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing browser reports that WebGL and WebGL2 are disabled and software rendering is forced.

question_patterns: Can you paste the actual console error and shader text rather than a screenshot?
What exact WebGL warnings and shader source are printed by the failing browser?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The console prints `CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL: loseContext: context lost`, `INVALID_OPERATION: delete: object does not belong to this context`, and `Shader compilation error`. The shader samples `uTextureSampler_0_S0` and computes a circle using `length((ucircle_S1_c0.xy - sk_FragCoord.xy) * ucircle_S1_c0.w)` before multiplying the texture output by the circle output.

question_patterns: Could you reduce the page to a minimal example and tell me if it still crashes?
Does a stripped-down build with just the avatar list reproduce the WebGL crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cut the page down to basically just the circle avatars — the reduced example still crashes the same way.

edges.comment: Thread c13-c23: the reporter supplied raw GPU and console output after explicit requests. The conclusion that the GPU process or Metal shader compiler is at fault is not placed in the user's answer. The reduced circle-avatar reproduction was then volunteered.

question_patterns: Can you reduce the example by testing the same network image flow with JPG, PNG, WebP, and GIF inputs?
Does the crash depend on the network image format?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested network images separately. JPG and JPEG make the app fail, while PNG, WebP, and GIF work. Changing the same image flow away from JPG makes the page render again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every tested image format, including PNG, WebP, GIF, and JPG, fails in the same way.
Both `.jpg` and `.jpeg` fail, while the same set of non-JPEG formats works.

edges.comment: Thread c29-c58: multiple affected users were folded into one simulated user side. Community reductions established the raw format comparison: browser-loaded network JPEGs trigger the failure, while PNG, WebP, and GIF do not.

question_patterns: Can you compile the profile or release build with `--dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false` and report whether it helps?
Please disable browser image decoding for a test build and try the same network JPEG.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This works for me. The release build compiled with `--dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false` renders the same JPEG case instead of going blank.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The build still goes blank with the same shader error when browser image decoding is disabled.

edges.comment: Thread c63-c65: this is a handler-initiated configuration measurement and therefore remains clarification-only. It verifies a temporary bypass, while the engineer separately warns that UI-thread image decoding can cause jank.

solution.intent: Enable Chrome's Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization flag and relaunch the browser to avoid the rendering failure.
solution.concrete_example: Open `chrome://flags`, set Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization to Enabled, and relaunch Chrome.

edges.comment: Thread c25-c35: the flag helped some affected users but was explicitly tried without success by another affected Intel Mac user, folded into the simulated user side. It is also not a deployable customer-facing fix, so it must not be treated as the reliable resolution.

solution.intent: Treat this as a Chromium ANGLE-on-Metal regression on Intel macOS, not a Flutter shader defect; have affected users update to a Chrome build containing the Chrome-side rollback or fix. Use disabled browser image decoding only as a temporary application-controlled workaround.
solution.concrete_example: Update affected Intel Mac users to Chrome 122.0.6261.129 or another build containing Chromium issue 328302269's correction, which disabled or reverted the problematic ANGLE Metal experiment. If an immediate app-side mitigation is required, build profile/release with `--dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false`, understanding that image decoding then runs on the UI thread and may cause jank.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied browser-version comparisons, GPU output, raw shader text, image-format tests, and update results. Engineers inferred that the crashing compilation path was inside Chromium's Skia/ANGLE Metal stack on Intel macOS rather than a shader authored by the Flutter application or Flutter's bundled CanvasKit. Chromium's disabling or reverting of the ANGLE-Metal experiment, followed by successful user verification, grounds that conclusion.

edges.comment: Reshaped (rule 4d): the fix is proposed here on pre-fix evidence; verification moves terminal-side.

question_patterns: Please update Chrome to the latest stable and tell me whether the page still crashes.
After updating the browser, could you reload the avatar page and report what happens?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can confirm it is working for me after the corrected Chrome rollout. The hosted example renders again, and other affected Intel Mac users confirmed that it is no longer affecting their setups.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The corrected Chrome version still loses the WebGL context and shows the same shader compilation error.
The same corrected rollout works on my Intel Mac under a later Chrome patch version.

edges.comment: Post-fix verification (neutral patterns; the fix is not named to the user).

solution.intent: Try the newer Chrome Beta (v123) to see whether the upstream fix has reached it.
solution.concrete_example: Could you try the v123 Beta and see if it resolves your issue too?

edges.comment: Real falsified attempt (c69-c70): v123 Beta still blank for the reporter.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as a Chromium ANGLE-on-Metal regression on Intel macOS that crashes or loses the GPU/WebGL context while compiling the relevant Skia shader path; it is not fundamentally a Flutter application shader or Flutter master/stable defect.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the Chrome channel and x86_64 specificity, raw GPU/context-loss and shader output, network-JPEG trigger, browser-image-decoding bypass, and successful corrected-Chrome verification.

The durable resolution must be updating to a Chrome build containing Chromium's rollback or fix for the Intel Mac ANGLE-Metal rollout; `BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false` may be offered only as a temporary workaround with its UI-thread decoding and jank risk.
Must not present enabling Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization as a reliable customer fix: it was not deployable by the app and an affected user explicitly reported that it did not work.
Must not require converting all JPEGs, abandoning CanvasKit, or upgrading Flutter as the root fix, although image conversion or another renderer may be mentioned as temporary mitigations.
Must treat the issue as resolved only after the reporter or another affected Intel Mac user verifies that the hosted application works in the corrected Chrome version.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Flutter developer who can publish reduced web reproductions, switch Flutter channels, compare browser versions, inspect `about:gpu`, paste shader logs, and test build-time defines, but relies on browser and engine specialists for low-level ANGLE/Metal diagnosis.
persona_hint.communication_style: Responsive, informal, and collaborative; provides concrete version and hardware details, tags participants directly, proposes hypotheses from reductions, and asks whether additional confirmation is needed before closing.
